title: Another Daily GLP-1 Pill Posts Double-Digit Weight Loss
hook: Aleniglipron, an experimental once-daily pill, helped people lose up to 12.1% of their body weight in 36 weeks — no injections, no fridge, no meal timing.
key_points: In a trial, aleniglipron produced up to 12.1% body-weight loss over 36 weeks.
It's a small molecule taken once daily, with or without food.
That's a contrast with injectables like Wegovy and Ozempic, which are peptides.
Small molecules are easier to manufacture at scale, which could ease supply and cost.
It's still experimental — not approved, and long-term safety data are limited.
content_html: The race to put GLP-1 weight loss in a pill has another entrant. In a trial reported by ScienceDaily, the experimental drug aleniglipron helped people with obesity or overweight lose as much as 12.1% of their body weight over 36 weeks.
extra_html:
What sets it apart is chemistry rather than the result. Wegovy and Ozempic are peptides — fragile enough that they're injected, and finicky to make. Aleniglipron is a small molecule, which means it survives the gut: one pill a day, with or without food, no refrigeration. Small molecules are also far easier to manufacture at scale, so a successful oral GLP-1 could relieve the supply crunches and high prices that have shaped this drug class from the start.

The usual caution applies. This is an experimental drug reported from a trial, not an approved treatment, and the questions that matter most for a medicine people may take for years — long-term safety, who keeps the weight off, side effects at scale — take longer to answer than 36 weeks.

related.title: A New Weight-Loss Pill Beats Oral Ozempic in a Major Trial
related.hook: Orforglipron, a once-daily weight-loss pill, outperformed oral semaglutide on weight loss and blood sugar in a major trial — and skips the refrigeration and meal-timing rules.

related.title: Why GLP-1 Drugs Don't Work for Everyone
related.hook: Scientists found genetic variants — carried by roughly 1 in 10 people — that seem to cause a kind of 'GLP-1 resistance,' making drugs like Ozempic less effective at controlling blood sugar.

related.title: Weight Loss That Lasts
related.hook: Crash diets win the first month and lose the year. Slow, steady loss built on habits you can actually keep is what stays off.

flashcards.explanation_html: Aleniglipron is a small molecule that can be swallowed once a day with or without food, whereas Wegovy and Ozempic are injectable peptide drugs.

flashcards.prompt: Why does 'small molecule' matter beyond convenience?
flashcards.back_html: Manufacturing. Small molecules are easier to produce at scale than peptides, which could ease the supply bottlenecks and costs that have dogged GLP-1 drugs.

flashcards.prompt: How much weight did trial participants lose, and over how long?
flashcards.back_html: Up to 12.1% of body weight in 36 weeks, in people with obesity or overweight. The drug is still experimental, not approved.
